body.statement: Does \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)\) determine \(\kappa_\alpha\) such that \(R_{N,\alpha}(u)/\min\{1,u^{-1/2}\}\to\kappa_\alpha\) uniformly on compact nondegenerate faces of \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{coll}}(p_T,\mathcal H)\), and can an inversion derived through \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{sharp}}\) attain it while retaining honesty at face transitions?
body.justification: The rate theorem does not determine the exact confidence-length constant or optimal test shape.
body.gap: Mikusheva studies invariant weak-IV geometry and Cai and Low sharp Gaussian moduli, but neither covers causal allocation-face transitions.
body.consumer: An exact constant would compare collections with similar rate indices but different finite-strength geometry.

obligation.what_is_open: A uniform Le Cam comparison and an ordered-modulus optimizer that remains honest when the active allocation face changes.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen local experiment is only a construction handle. The proved quadratic modulus fixes the rate and local testing cost, but it does not control higher-order likelihood terms uniformly near face transitions or solve the bounded-parameter Gaussian confidence-set optimization.
obligation.attempted: The fixed-face quadratic program was dualized explicitly and reduced to a Gaussian interval-rule optimization. This does not identify a universal exact constant because the required uniform experiment convergence and transition-stable optimizer are additional claims.
obligation.partial_result:
On any fixed allocation face the quadratic program has the computable representation
\[
 V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)=
 \sum_x\frac{p_T(x)^2}
 {\sum_{s:x\in\mathcal H_s}n_sp_s(x)/q_{sx}(\theta_T)},
\]
and the local Gaussian testing cost for displacement \(h\) is
\(h^2T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)/2\). Thus, if the asserted Le Cam convergence is established, a facewise sharp constant is the value of the explicit optimization over measurable interval rules \(C\) in that Gaussian experiment:
\[
 \inf_C\ \sup_{t\in[-1,1]}E_t\ell(C)
 \quad\text{subject to}\quad
 \inf_{t\in[-1,1]}\Pr_t\{t\in C\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
The rate results alone neither identify this value nor prove that an optimizer remains uniformly honest when the active allocation face changes.
